findings.title: Equal `order()` values make provider selection depend on classpath order
findings.description: The old `detectProvider` threw when more than one `CryptoProvider` was on the classpath. The diff removes that check and sorts by `order()` instead (line 57). `DefaultCryptoProvider` (line 84), `FIPS1402Provider` (line 115) and `WildFlyElytronProvider` (line 77) all return 200. If two of them are present, the winner is whichever `ServiceLoader` returns first, with no error. The FIPS-versus-default case matters most: if the non-FIPS provider wins, FIPS mode runs without any signal. Quarkus is protected in practice. `KeycloakRecorder.setCryptoProvider` (`quarkus/runtime/src/main/java/org/keycloak/quarkus/runtime/KeycloakRecorder.java:214`) sets the provider explicitly, and `IgnoredArtifacts` drops one of the two jars per FIPS mode. The non-Quarkus `init()` path has no guard now. Keep throwing when the top two providers share an order, or give FIPS a strictly higher value. Also, no test covers the new selection behaviour, and the debug call at line 69 passes a built string as the format argument. Use `logger.debugf("Ignored crypto providers: %s", ...)` instead.

findings.title: `order()` added as an abstract method on a public SPI
findings.description: `CryptoProvider` is an extension point loaded through `ServiceLoader` (the services file is in `authz/client`). The new `int order();` has no default, so any external implementation stops compiling. Already-compiled implementations throw `AbstractMethodError` once `order()` is invoked, which happens as soon as a second provider is present. All four in-repo implementers were updated and a repo-wide search found no others. Consider `default int order() { return 0; }` so that explicit providers still win.

findings.title: ECDSA DER→RS conversion never checks the signature length
findings.description: `concatenatedRSToASN1DER` copies `[0, len)` and `[len, 2·len)` with no check on `signature.length`. Extra trailing bytes are silently dropped and the trimmed value is re-encoded and verified. `ECDSASignatureVerifierContext.verify` (`core/src/main/java/org/keycloak/crypto/ECDSASignatureVerifierContext.java:29-31`) passes the raw token signature with no length check. Where this provider is active, an ES256 signature with extra bytes appended verifies, and RFC 7518 §3.4 fixes the signature length. Short input fails with `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException`, which the verifier wraps as `VerificationException`, so only the over-long case is a problem. `BCECDSACryptoProvider.java:34-35` has the same gap, so it is inherited. This new copy is the place to add `if (signature.length != signLength) throw new IOException(...)`.

findings.title: The round-trip test cannot detect wrong conversions
findings.description: The helper asserts only that `asn1derToConcatenatedRS → concatenatedRSToASN1DER → asn1derToConcatenatedRS` is self-consistent (line 56). Two gaps follow. First, the key is `KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC").genKeyPair()` (line 42) with no curve, so the key is not tied to ES256/384/512. For a key larger than the algorithm expects, `integerToBytes` truncates R and S, the re-encoded DER carries the truncated values, and the second parse returns the same bytes, so the assertion passes on wrong output. Second, nothing checks that the re-encoded DER verifies with `Signature.verify`, or matches the JDK's `sign` bytes, which is the actual contract. Initialize the generator with a matching `ECGenParameterSpec` per algorithm, assert `Signature.verify` on the re-encoded DER, and assert `assertArrayEquals(sign, asn1Des)`. No test covers malformed input.

findings.title: Dead statements in `concatenatedRSToASN1DER`
findings.description: Two statements create encoders and discard them. The real encoding happens at lines 117-121. Remove them.

findings.title: `getBouncyCastleProvider()` returns a JDK keystore provider, not BouncyCastle
findings.description: The method returns `KeyStore.getInstance(getDefaultType()).getProvider()`, which is usually SUN. `BouncyIntegration.PROVIDER` is therefore set to that name. In the authz client's classpath the only reader I found is the debug log at `CryptoIntegration.java:34`, so the impact is small. Returning `null`, as `WildFlyElytronProvider` does, is the simpler fix. `BouncyIntegration.loadProvider` already handles null (`common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/util/BouncyIntegration.java:35-38`).

findings.title: ASN.1 decoder accepts loose structure and throws unchecked exceptions
findings.description: `readInteger` with indefinite length (0x80) gets `-1` from `readLength`, then `read(-1)` throws `NegativeArraySizeException` (line 72). A zero-length INTEGER throws `NumberFormatException` from `new BigInteger(empty)` (line 73). Both escape a method that declares `IOException`. The only in-repo caller on this path is the signing side, which feeds JDK output and wraps `Exception` (`core/.../ECDSASignatureSignerContext.java:33-35`), so this is latent. `readSequence` (lines 55-61) does not check that child elements stay inside the declared length or that there are no trailing bytes. `readTagNumber` compares only the low five bits (line 94), so the class and constructed bits are ignored. Either tighten these checks or document the parser as permissive.

findings.title: Hamcrest is declared but unused
findings.description: The only test imports `org.junit.Assert` and `org.junit.Test` (`ECDSAAlgorithmTest.java:27-28`). Nothing imports `org.hamcrest`. Remove it or use it.

findings.title: `AuthzClient.create` now mutates JVM-wide crypto state
findings.description: `CryptoIntegration.init` is process-global and first-caller-wins, and it uses `AuthzClient`'s classloader. If the authz client initializes first and no higher-order provider is visible from that loader, the process is left with `AuthzClientCryptoProvider`, where most methods throw `UnsupportedOperationException`. This is not a regression, since before the diff nothing initialized the provider and such calls failed with `IllegalStateException`. The admin CLI uses the same pattern (`integration/client-cli/admin-cli/.../Globals.java:44`), so it is a known trade-off. A Javadoc note on the public `create` methods would help.

findings.title: Unrelated whitespace-only edits
findings.description: Trailing whitespace was removed here, and in `DefaultCryptoProvider.java` and `FIPS1402Provider.java`. These edits are unrelated to the feature and add review noise. Consider splitting them out.

findings.title: Module artifact is described as testsuite-only
findings.description: The module that now contains `AuthzClient`, the new services registration and the new provider is `keycloak-authz-client-tests`. Its description says it is "NOT supposed to be used by the 3rd party applications" and points to `org.keycloak:keycloak-authz-client`. In this checkout I found no POM that declares `keycloak-authz-client`, and the root `pom.xml:1055` references only the `-tests` artifact. This predates the diff, but the new `ServiceLoader` registration changes global crypto behaviour for whoever ships this module, so confirm the publishing target.

findings.title: DER↔RS conversion now exists in four copies
findings.description: The same conversion lives in `BCECDSACryptoProvider`, `BCFIPSECDSACryptoProvider`, `ElytronECDSACryptoProvider` and now `AuthzClientCryptoProvider`. A hand-written ASN.1 codec is reasonable here, since the authz client should not depend on BouncyCastle. It is still a fourth copy to keep in sync, and it carries the gaps described above. `ASN1Decoder` is package-private, yet its `create`, `readSequence` and `readInteger` methods are `public` (lines 45, 49, 65), which is inconsistent.

findings.title: All in-repo `CryptoProvider` implementations implement `order()`
findings.description: `DefaultCryptoProvider` (82-85), `WildFlyElytronProvider` (75-78), `FIPS1402Provider` (113-116) and `AuthzClientCryptoProvider` (69-72) each implement `order()`. A repo-wide search for `implements`, `extends` or `new CryptoProvider` found no other implementers, so the abstract method compiles everywhere in this checkout. External implementers are covered by the finding above.

findings.title: ECDSA signing does not reach the authz provider's unsupported methods
findings.description: `ECDSASignatureSignerContext.sign` calls `super.sign`, which gets its `Signature` from the JDK directly (line 48), and then converts with `ECDSAAlgorithm.asn1derToConcatenatedRS`. So ES* signing from the authz client needs only the conversion, and that conversion is implemented. The verifier falls back to `CryptoIntegration.getProvider().getSignature` only when the JDK lookup fails (`AsymmetricSignatureVerifierContext.java:60-63`).
